title: Ringed and abstract native K-flat tensor models with localization transformations
statement:
Let $(C,J)$ be a site small relative to its module universe [def-weil-pbc-sites-and-cohomology, def-weil-size-convention], $R$ a sheaf of commutative rings, and $\mathcal M=\operatorname{Mod}(R)$ [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category], with its closed symmetric sheaf tensor [def-pur-sheaf-tensor-product]. Suppose a functor from $\mathcal M$ to its flat objects and a natural epimorphism from that functor to the identity have been fixed (functorial flat resolutions). Use unbounded integer cochain complexes, the homotopy category $K(R)$, and its quasi-isomorphism localization $q:K(R)\to D(R)$ [def-weil-abstract-derived-category]. All tensor complexes are signed direct-sum totals [def-pc-tensor-complex-sheaves]. Call a complex acyclic when all its cohomology sheaves vanish. Use acyclic-test K-flatness [def-pc-kflat-complex] and two-sided quasi-isomorphism-test K-flatness [def-sfb-preserves-kflat-quasi-iso]. Let $\mathcal P$ be the full homotopy subcategory of acyclic-test K-flat complexes with flat terms [def-pc-flat-sheaf-modules].
Let $B_R$ be the independently constructed ringed-site K-flat derived tensor, with model maps $r^R_{P,Q}:q\operatorname{Tot}(P\otimes_R Q)\cong B_R(qP,qQ)$ for $P,Q\in\mathcal P$ [lem-weil-pbc-site-derived-tensor-descent]. Give it the associator and both unitors induced from unsigned cochain reassociation and the regular degree-zero complex [lem-sf-ringed-derived-closed-symmetric-monoidal]. Let $B_a$ be the native tensor of the abstract derived monoidal construction [lem-sfb-derived-monoidal], using two-sided K-flat complexes, with its canonical model maps $r^a$ and its constraints induced from complexes. Write $\varepsilon^R_{U,V}:B_R(qU,qV)\to q\operatorname{Tot}(U\otimes_R V)$ and $\varepsilon^a$ for the canonical derived-to-ordinary transformations obtained from the respective K-flat resolution constructions; these are the inverses of the model maps on resolving pairs.
The two tests for K-flatness are equivalent for every complex of $R$-module sheaves, including those without flat terms. There is a unique natural isomorphism $w:B_a\cong B_R$ with
$$w_{qP,qQ}\,r^a_{P,Q}=r^R_{P,Q}\qquad(P,Q\in\mathcal P).$$
For every pair of complexes $U,V$ it satisfies
$$\varepsilon^R_{U,V}\,w_{qU,qV}=\varepsilon^a_{U,V}.$$
Each localization transformation is invertible whenever either $U$ or $V$ is K-flat, even if it has nonflat terms; on every K-flat pair the same normalization $w\,r^a=r^R$ holds for the corresponding model maps. With unit comparison the identity of $q(R[0])$, $w$ identifies the two associators and both unitors on all derived objects. Thus a comparison normalized using the ringed model and compatible with its localization transformation on all complex pairs is normalized also in the abstract native model on every K-flat pair. No boundedness assumption or identification of site object and morphism universes is imposed. Composition is read right to left.

proof.text: Use the native kFlat theorem and Mathlib kFlat_quotient_obj_iff to turn acyclic-test K-flatness into the two-sided quasi-isomorphism test. Conversely apply the right tensor test to the quasi-isomorphism from the zero complex to an acyclic complex; tensor sends the zero complex to zero, so its target is acyclic. No flat-term condition enters either implication.

proof.text: The proved kFlatLocalization helper of RingedDerivedTensorHomAdjunction says that the inclusion of all acyclic-test K-flat complexes followed by Q is a localization. On its product with itself compose the inverse native comparison with T.comparison and use Localization.liftNatIso. Its restriction is the prescribed comparison on every K-flat pair. To detect equality on flat-term resolving pairs, choose the existing K-flat resolutions of arbitrary complex inputs, use naturality and cancel the images of the quasi-isomorphism augmentations. Localization.natTrans_ext then detects equality on arbitrary derived inputs.

source.place: Tags 06YP, 06YS, 06YU, 0FPQ and 0FPT; comparison by localization and naturality, expanded by F5.

proof.text: Assemble the native localization tensorator as a natural transformation and compose it with the inverse comparison to construct the ringed localization transformation. On resolving pairs it equals the inverse ringed model map. Resolve arbitrary pairs and cancel the ringed tensor of the augmentation isomorphisms to show uniqueness of a transformation with this normalization. This proves the all-complex equation. Native isIso_mu proves invertibility whenever either factor is K-flat, and the comparison transfers it to the ringed transformation. For the one-K-flat representative normalization, resolve both inputs and combine the naturality squares of the two model maps and the comparison; invertibility of the native model maps and the derived augmentation tensors makes the localized ordinary tensor map cancellable.

source.place: Tags 06YP, 06YS, 06YU, 0FPQ and 0FPT; comparison by localization and naturality, expanded by F5.

proof.text: Identify the cochain associator and unitor maps in hc with the native complex constraints. Reuse the proved ordinaryAssociator_unique and ordinaryRightUnitor_unique helpers from RingedOrdinaryEvaluationLocalization for those two identities; degreewise tensor-generator extensionality proves the left unitor identity, with nonzero unit degrees vanishing. On triples of K-flat representatives substitute the model comparison equations into the two associator squares, use naturality to commute the comparison past the inner model maps, and cancel the outer and inner native model isomorphisms. The outer pairs require only one K-flat factor, so tensor-closure of flat-term resolutions is unnecessary. Equality of the two natural transformations extends along the triple product of the K-flat localization. The same argument, using one-K-flat unit pairs and cancelling their native model maps, proves both unitor equations on K-flat representatives and extends along the localization to all objects.
